records.title: 1860 U.S. census: John “Dorsey,” blacksmith, with Catherine and baby John, Ward 5, Providence
records.text: 1860 census, Providence Ward 5, enumerated July 1860; dwelling 1412, family 2184. Written on the page as Dorsey (Ancestry also indexes it as D’Arcy). John, 30, male, blacksmith, born Ireland. Catherine, 31, female, marked as married within the year. Patrick, 15, male, born Rhode Island. Johanna, 10, female. William, 3, male. Catherine, 5, female. John, 7/12 (seven months), male, born Rhode Island. Why this is very likely the Darcy family: same ward as the 1875 Darcy household; father a blacksmith in both; the children Catherine (5 → 19), William (3 → 16) and John (7 months → 15) are 14, 13 and about 14½ years older (the adults’ ages fit less well: John 30 → 40, Catherine 31 → 38, then 60 in 1880); and a 7-month-old in July 1860 fits John F. Darcy’s birth on December 8, 1859. Patrick and Johanna, older than the marriage, may be Catherine’s children from an earlier marriage (unproven). John F. Darcy’s birth year is itself in conflict: 1859 in late records, December 1862 in the 1900 census, and about 1861–62 from his marriage ages.
records.ref: 1860 United States Federal Census, Providence Ward 5, Providence County, Rhode Island, page 155 (Ancestry collection 7667, record 34906765, image 4293578_00403; NARA M653)

records.title: Marriage of Atkinson Nodders and Mary (Mariam) Ragan, St. Patrick’s, Oldham, Lancashire

records.title: Marriage of Édouard Bonvouloir (Deslières) and Célina Dufresne, Bolton, Quebec
records.text: No. 11. November 25, 1867, after three banns at this mission and two at Sutton (the third dispensed by the Vicar General, Crevier): Édouard Bonvouloir, day laborer, living in this mission, a minor, son of the late Édouard Bonvouloir dit Delier(?) and of Elsiste(?) Brunelle, of Brome Corner in the mission of Sutton; and Célina Dufresne, a minor, daughter of Bazile Dufresne, day laborer, and of Françoise Rochichaud(?), of this mission. Married with their parents’ consent, in the presence of Bazile Dufresne, father of the bride, and Isidore Tocelin(?), standing as father to the groom. Signed Célina Dufresne, B. Dufresne(?), Louis Decelles. These are Constance’s great-grandparents (Constance → Eugenie → Julia → Édouard and Célina): Édouard and Célina were the parents of her grandmother Julia. Bonvouloir is the family’s second name (a French-Canadian “dit” name) alongside Deslières.
records.ref: Quebec, Canada, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection); St-Étienne-de-Bolton, 1867, images 9–10 of 12

records.title: Margaret’s widowed mother marries James H. Stewart, Peterborough, New Hampshire, December 23, 1869
records.text: New Hampshire marriage record (front): Groom James H. Stewart; bride Mary Regan; both residing in Peterboro, N.H.; groom 22, bride 26; white; groom’s occupation spinner; groom born Scotland, bride born England; married by Ezra M. Smith of Peterboro, Justice of the Peace, December 23, 1869, at Peterboro. (Back): groom’s father A. Stewart, keeper of a public house, born Scotland; bride’s father John Regan, brick mason, born England. Copy certified 1905. Evidence that this bride was Margaret Jane Nodders’s mother (indirect; the card names no earlier husband or child, and the number-of-marriage and widowed fields are blank): she married under her maiden name Regan; her age (26, born about 1843), her English birth and her Regan maiden name all match the Mary E. Regan who married Atkinson Nodders in 1862; and in 1910 and 1915 the Darcys’ household includes the widow “Mary E. Stewart,” mother-in-law. Conflicts still to resolve: this bride’s father was born in England, but in 1910 Mary E. Stewart gave her father’s birthplace as Ireland; James, 22 in 1869, is 36 in the 1880 Fall River census (should be 32–33); Margaret is 10 there (should be 11); and Margaret’s father is named Henry (1888), William (1942) and Atkinson (1862, 1866). If the identification holds, it would explain why one record calls Margaret “Stewart.”
records.ref: New Hampshire, U.S., Marriage Records, 1700–1974, Stebbins–Sweeney (Ancestry collection 61836, record 200702, images 61836_01_0717-03312 and -03313); New Hampshire Marriage Records Index (collection 2554, records 200427, 701585)

records.title: 1875 Rhode Island census: John Darcy, blacksmith, and family, Ward 5, Providence
records.text: Census of the City of Providence, June 1, 1875, district 45, Ward 5, volume 15, page 223, household 84. John Darcy, head, 40, male, married, born in Ireland, Irish parentage, blacksmith. Cath. Darcy, wife, 38, married, born in Ireland, housekeeper; marked as unable to read or write. Wm. Darcy, son, 16, born in Providence, laborer. John Darcy, son, 15, born in Providence, jeweler. Cath. Darcy, daughter, 19, born in Providence, spooler in a cotton mill. On the line just above: Wm. Cannon, 17, step son, born in Providence, jeweler (the household number 84 is written on John Darcy’s line, so whether this stepson belongs to the Darcys is not certain from the image). The 15-year-old jeweler John is Constance’s grandfather John Francis Darcy (born December 8, 1859; still a jeweler when he married in 1884 and 1888).
records.ref: Rhode Island, U.S., State Censuses, 1865–1935: 1875, Providence, Ward 5 (Ancestry collection 4721, records 308712–308716, image 41271_307539-00447)

records.title: 1880 U.S. census: James Stewart’s household in Fall River, with daughters Sarah and Margaret (probably the Nodders girls)
records.text: James Stewart, 36, head, born Scotland; Mary Stewart, 38, wife, born England; Sarah, 17; Margrette, 10, daughter, born Massachusetts, at school; Connie, 7; Charles, 5. This is a candidate only. It matches Margaret Jane’s age, her Massachusetts birth and her mother Mary’s English birth, and it would explain why her daughter Ethel’s death certificate gives her maiden name as Stewart. Nothing yet proves this is her family. UPDATE: now very likely the right family. Margaret’s mother Mary Regan married James H. Stewart, born Scotland, in December 1869; Margaret’s sister Sarah Ann Nodders married in Fall River in 1882; and the ages (James 36 born Scotland, Mary 38 born England, Margaret 10 born Massachusetts) fit. Age conflicts remain: James should be about 32–33 and Margaret 11.
records.ref: 1880 United States Federal Census

John F., son, 19, single, works for jeweler, born Rhode Island; father and mother born Ireland. Her husband John Darcy, the blacksmith of 1860 and 1875, had died by 1880. Five years later John F. Darcy’s first wife Ellen died at 78 Borden Street, two doors away.

records.title: 1900 U.S. census: the Darcy family, 62 Orchard Street, East Providence
records.text: Sheet 24, dwelling 652, family 574 (line numbers 59–66). John Darcy, head, born Dec 1862 in Rhode Island, 37, married 12 years; both parents born in Ireland; street railroad conductor; the owned/rented column reads R (rented). Ancestry’s index says “Own”; the image says rented. Margaret J., wife, born Feb 1869 in Massachusetts, 31, married 12 years, mother of 6 children, 6 living; her father and mother both born in England. Children, all born in Rhode Island: Albert B., son, Nov 1888, 11, at school; Loretta, daughter, Aug 1890, 9, at school; Lillian A., daughter, July 1892, 7, at school; Ethel M., daughter, Nov 1894, 5, at school; Mary S., daughter, Sept 1895 (as written), 4; Harvey F., son, Apr 1898, 2. (Ancestry’s index reads the head as John T. and Ethel as 7; the image reads John F. and Ethel 5.) Neighbors: Owen Finnegan family at 62 Orchard (stationary engineer). Constance’s father Albert is the 11-year-old son.

records.title: 1910 U.S. census: the Darcys of East Providence, with Margaret’s mother, the widow Mary E. Stewart
records.text: 1910 census, East Providence town, enumeration district 99, sheet 12A, dwelling 207, family 277, enumerated in April 1910. John F. Darcy, head, 47, married 22 years, born Rhode Island, father born Ireland, mother born England (as written), starter, electric railroad. Margaret J., wife, 41, married 22 years, mother of 7 children, 7 living, born Massachusetts, both parents born England. Children: Albert B., son, 21, apprentice, monotype; Lilly A., daughter, 17, stenographer, office; Ethel M., daughter, 16, winder, wire mill; Mary S., daughter, 14, errand girl, department store; Harold F., 11 (written “daughter” in error); Olive R., daughter, 8. Loretta L. Hogan, daughter, 19, married under a year, and her husband William J. Hogan, son-in-law, 24, born New Hampshire, letter carrier, post office. Mary E. Stewart, mother-in-law, 68, widowed, mother of 7 children with 3 living, born England, father born Ireland, mother born England, came to the United States in 1862. This is the record that ties the name Stewart to Margaret: her mother lived with her in 1910 as Mrs. Mary E. Stewart, a widow. (A member tree on Ancestry calls her Mary Elizabeth Regan, 1842–1916; that is not a record.)
records.ref: 1910 United States Federal Census, East Providence, Providence County, Rhode Island, ED 99, sheet 12A (Ancestry collection 7884, record 156895093, image 4450037_00468; NARA T624)

records.title: 290 Westminster Street was the Lapham Building, home to several beauty shops

Inc., room 510. Constance worked as a hairdresser in this building, in room 506 in 1937 and in room 402 (printed “290 Wash”) in 1938. Pictures: an early-1900s colored postcard captioned “Corner of Westminster and Mathewson Sts. showing Lapham Building, Providence, R.I.,” with LAPHAM BUILDING lettered over the entrance; and an undivided-back era postcard captioned “Westminster Street — Providence, R.I.,” showing streetcars and crowds on Westminster Street. Both postcards date from decades before Constance worked there and are shown for the building and street, not for her.

timeline: Julie Deslières, Constance’s grandmother, is born at Sutton, Quebec.
Albert Blake Darcy, Constance’s father, is born at Rumford, East Providence.
Julie marries Thimothée Deslières at St-André, Sutton.
Eugenie Emma Delaire, Constance’s mother, is born.
Julie, widowed, enters the United States at Newport, Vermont.
Julie and Eugenie are living at 53 Jewett Street, Providence.
Albert Darcy and Eugenie Delaire marry in Providence.
Constance Eugenie Darcy is born at 410 Smith Street, Providence.
Her brother, Albert Norman, is born in Taunton, Massachusetts.
The census finds the family on Alms Street, Providence.
The state census finds them at 29 Burgess Avenue, East Providence.
Albert takes out a license to marry Theresa B. Sullivan.
Constance, 17, is in school; her mother, divorced, heads the household at 111 Pratt Street.
Her grandmother Julia dies; she is buried in lot 84 at Saint Ann, Cranston.
Directory: Constance is a student, at 7 Beacon Avenue.
State census card: Constance is a hairdresser, at 75 Abbott Street.
Her first daughter, Eugenie Elizabeth, is born in Attleboro, Massachusetts.
She marries Laurence Brown Douglas in Birmingham, Alabama.
The census finds Laurence, Constance and Eugenie on Valencia Street, San Francisco.
Constance and Laurence cross from Canada at Blaine, Washington.
Laurence’s naturalization petition in Pittsburgh names Constance and two daughters.
Her brother, A. Norman Darcy, dies.
Her father, Albert Blake Darcy, dies.
Directory: Constance is a nurse at Roger Williams General Hospital.
Laurence dies at St. Joseph’s Hospital, Providence.
Warwick directory: widow, nurse, 119 Phillips Avenue.
Constance dies, at 81; she is buried in lot 84 at Saint Ann, Cranston.
